sourceNote: Compiled from public company disclosures, published platform documentation, academic research on recommender systems, and investigative reporting. Static dataset — never live-accessed, never connected to the user's own accounts.

platforms.name: TikTok
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising (in-feed ads, branded effects), live-stream gifting commissions, and TikTok Shop commerce fees.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: The For You feed is interest-based rather than social-graph-based. Each video is shown to a small test audience, then promoted or dropped based on completion rate, rewatches, shares, comments and likes — in roughly that order of weight. Completion rate matters most, which is why videos are short and front-load a hook. Because it does not need your friends list to work, it can profile a new account's tastes within dozens of videos.
knownDarkPatterns: infinite scroll with no stopping cue
streak and gifting mechanics on LIVE
platforms.privacyImplications: Collects watch duration per video, keystroke cadence, device and network identifiers, and contact lists if granted. Watch-time signals are unusually granular because they drive the core ranking model.

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising, primarily behaviourally targeted; plus creator commerce and subscriptions.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: Separate ranking models per surface. Feed weighs how likely you are to linger, like, comment or save, mixing followed accounts with recommended ones. Reels leans almost entirely on predicted watch-through and shares, so it behaves much like TikTok. Explore is pure recommendation. Ranking optimises predicted engagement, not chronology — so 'what you see first' reflects predicted reaction, not recency.
knownDarkPatterns: engagement-optimised ordering presented as a feed of friends
appearance-comparison surfaces (Explore, Reels) shown by default
platforms.privacyImplications: Shares an advertising graph with Facebook and WhatsApp. Off-platform activity can be linked via the Meta pixel on third-party sites unless limited in settings.

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising — the majority of Meta's revenue — sold on detailed interest, behaviour and lookalike targeting.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: News Feed scores thousands of candidate posts per visit on predicted meaningful interaction: comments and reshares weigh more heavily than passive views. Groups and Reels are injected as growth surfaces. Content that provokes reply-chains tends to spread, which is a known amplifier of conflict-shaped posts.
knownDarkPatterns: default-on data sharing across Meta properties
platforms.privacyImplications: Extensive off-platform tracking through pixels and SDKs; ad targeting can be derived from behaviour you never entered on the platform.

platforms.name: YouTube
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising split with creators, Premium subscriptions, channel memberships.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: Recommendations optimise for predicted satisfied watch time across a session, not a single video. The 'up next' and homepage models draw on your history, similar viewers' histories, and video metadata. Longer sessions are the objective, which structurally favours series, cliffhangers and sequels.
knownDarkPatterns: mid-roll ad density on long content
Shorts feed as an infinite scroll inside a long-form app
platforms.privacyImplications: Watch history is tied to your Google account by default and informs advertising across Google properties unless history controls are turned off.

platforms.name: X (formerly Twitter)
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising plus paid verification and subscription tiers.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: The default 'For You' timeline mixes followed accounts with out-of-network posts ranked by a predicted-engagement model; replies and reposts weigh heavily, and paid accounts receive reach weighting. A reverse-chronological 'Following' tab remains available and is a meaningfully calmer surface.
knownDarkPatterns: trending module as a manufactured-urgency surface
algorithmic tab set as default over chronological
platforms.privacyImplications: Public-by-default posting; engagement and follow graphs are visible to third parties and widely scraped.

platforms.name: Snapchat
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising, Snapchat+ subscriptions, AR lens partnerships.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: Friend content is largely relationship-ordered; Discover and Spotlight are algorithmic and watch-time driven. Snap Map surfaces location among mutual friends when enabled.
platforms.privacyImplications: Location sharing and streak mechanics generate a continuous behavioural record; 'disappearing' refers to the recipient's view, not to deletion from all systems.

platforms.name: Reddit
platforms.revenueModel: Advertising, Premium subscriptions, and data licensing to AI companies.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: Ranking is community-scoped and largely vote-based, with time decay — early votes have outsized influence on what reaches a front page. The Home feed blends subscribed subreddits with recommendations. Moderation and culture vary sharply per community.
knownDarkPatterns: early-vote lottery that rewards posting at peak hours
platforms.privacyImplications: Pseudonymous rather than anonymous — a long comment history is often enough to identify someone. Public content is licensed for AI training.

platforms.name: LinkedIn
platforms.revenueModel: Recruiter and sales subscriptions, advertising, and Premium memberships — the majority of revenue comes from paid tools rather than ads.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: Ranks on predicted professional engagement, favouring dwell time and comment threads. Rewards a recognisable register (personal-story-into-business-lesson), which is why the feed's writing style feels uniform.
knownDarkPatterns: profile-completeness and 'who viewed you' nudges gated behind Premium
platforms.privacyImplications: Your profile is a career-visible record; activity can be seen by employers and recruiters, and viewing others is often disclosed to them.

platforms.name: Threads
platforms.revenueModel: Currently minimal direct monetisation; strategically an engagement and advertising surface for Meta.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: The default feed is heavily recommendation-driven, surfacing accounts you do not follow. A following-only feed is available. Bootstrapped from the Instagram graph.
knownDarkPatterns: recommendation feed as default over following
account creation coupled to Instagram, making standalone deletion awkward
platforms.privacyImplications: Shares identity and interest signals with the Instagram/Meta graph.

platforms.name: Discord
platforms.revenueModel: Nitro subscriptions, server boosts, and cosmetic sales — not an advertising-first business.
platforms.algorithmicFeed: Largely non-algorithmic: content is chronological within channels you join. Attention pressure comes from real-time presence and notifications rather than ranking.
platforms.privacyImplications: Message history persists in servers indefinitely and is visible to server staff; DMs are not end-to-end encrypted.
